evals.prompt: I'm implementing a full CRUD feature for 'tasks' (create, list, edit, delete) across a database, an API, and a UI. Using incremental implementation, should I build all the database work first, then all the API endpoints, then all the UI screens (horizontal), or should I slice differently? Explain the recommended slicing approach and why.
evals.expected_output: Recommends vertical slicing -- one complete end-to-end path (e.g. 'create a task' through DB+API+UI) per slice -- over building each layer completely before moving to the next.

assertions.text: Recommends vertical slicing by name or description
Explicitly advises against building layer by layer across the whole feature

evals.prompt: While implementing a task that only requires adding a new API endpoint, I notice an unrelated file has an unused import and some outdated comments nearby. Per incremental implementation's scope discipline rule, should I fix these while I'm in the area, and if not, what should I do instead?
evals.expected_output: States these should not be fixed as part of this task (out of scope) and should instead be noted/flagged for a separate task, not silently cleaned up.

assertions.text: Says not to fix it as part of the current task
Recommends noting it for a separate task rather than silently ignoring it

evals.prompt: I need to merge a partially-built 'bulk export' feature to the main branch in small increments so my commits stay small, but the feature isn't ready for real users yet. What incremental-implementation technique should I use to merge safely without exposing an incomplete feature, and when should it be added relative to the first commit?
evals.expected_output: Recommends a feature flag that gates the incomplete feature, added starting with the very first commit that introduces the incomplete path, not added later.

assertions.text: States it should be present from the first commit, not added later
